text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Nambian construction industry has reached agreement on a minimum wage with the Metal and Allied Workers Union (Manwu), to be observed by all companies operating in the country. The hourly wage for non-qualified workers has been set at N$3.80. The move is an attempt to create a level playing field in the industry amid claims that Chinese building companies have been paying very low wages.
- The Chinese government has donated machinery worth N$1 million for use in Nambia's industrial parks. The assistance includes 33 tonnes of metal fabrication equipment.

- Fuel prices in Nambia have increased with effect from Wednesday, with the cost of petrol rising by 13 cents per litre and that of diesel by 14 cents. At the same time a road transport subsidy is introduced to keep fuel prices in outlying areas such as the Caprivi strip in check. Higher international prices for crude oil are also responsible for the rise.

- Petrol and diesel fuel prices have increased as from Wednesday by 13 and 14 cents respectively, in towns with large fuel depots. The increases at garages in outlying towns will be offset by a fuel transport subsidy.
